entries.appliesTo: food retailers (>=15,000 sq ft selling tax-exempt food) and third-party food delivery service providers (dynamic-pricing / surveillance-data prohibitions); merchants generally (algorithmic-pricing disclosure)

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 13-322(C) — 'UNLESS THE MERCHANT INCLUDES WITH THE ADVERTISEMENT, PROMOTION, LABEL, OR OTHER COMMUNICATION A CLEAR AND CONSPICUOUS DISCLOSURE WITH THE FOLLOWING STATEMENT: "THIS PRICE WAS SET BY AN ALGORITHM OR BY USING YOUR PERSONAL DATA"'

exposure.enforcer: consumer-protection-division (enforcement under Subtitle 4, Maryland Consumer Protection Act); private right of action expressly excluded

sources.prohibition: § 13-321(B)(2) — 'A FOOD RETAILER OR THIRD-PARTY FOOD DELIVERY SERVICE PROVIDER MAY NOT: (I) ENGAGE IN DYNAMIC PRICING TO SET A HIGHER PRICE FOR FOOD THAT IS EXEMPT FROM THE SALE AND USE TAX IN ACCORDANCE WITH § 11-206(C) OF THE TAX - GENERAL ARTICLE FOR A SPECIFIC CONSUMER; OR (II) USE SURVEILLANCE PERSONAL DATA TO SET A HIGHER PRICE'
sources.disclosure: § 13-322(C) — 'A MERCHANT MAY NOT SET THE PRICE OF A CONSUMER GOOD OR SERVICE USING DYNAMIC PRICING OR PERSONAL DATA AND DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY ADVERTISE OR PROMOTE, INCLUDE ON A LABEL, OR PUBLISH ANY OTHER COMMUNICATION CONTAINING THE PRICE, UNLESS THE MERCHANT INCLUDES ... A CLEAR AND CONSPICUOUS DISCLOSURE'
sources.enforcer: § 13-321(D)(1) / § 13-322(D)(1) — 'BEFORE INITIATING AN ENFORCEMENT ACTION UNDER SUBTITLE 4 OF THIS TITLE FOR A VIOLATION OF THIS SECTION, THE DIVISION SHALL ISSUE A NOTICE OF VIOLATION TO THE ALLEGED VIOLATOR'; § 13-321(E) — 'THIS SECTION MAY NOT BE CONSTRUED TO AUTHORIZE A PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION UNDER THIS SECTION OR ANY OTHER LAW'
sources.cureDays: § 13-321(D)(2) / § 13-322(D)(2) — 'THE DIVISION SHALL PROVIDE THE ALLEGED VIOLATOR 45 DAYS AFTER THE NOTICE OF VIOLATION IS RECEIVED TO CURE THE VIOLATION'

flags: AI appears only inside the dynamic-pricing definition: § 13-321(A)(3)(I) — 'INCLUDING THROUGH THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE OR MODELS THAT RETRAIN OR RECALIBRATE BASED ON RECEIVED INFORMATION IN NEAR REAL-TIME'; the prohibitions reach personalized pricing from personal data whether or not AI is used
prohibition param is lossy: the text bans both personalized dynamic pricing (personal-data-based, incl. AI) and surveillance-personal-data pricing; 'surveillance-pricing' is the closest single enum

§ 13-321(C) additionally prohibits food retailers/delivery providers from using 'PROTECTED CLASS DATA TO OFFER, ADVERTISE, OR SELL A CONSUMER GOOD OR SERVICE' where it has 'THE EFFECT OF WITHHOLDING OR DENYING FROM THE CONSUMER AN ACCOMMODATION, AN ADVANTAGE, OR A PRIVILEGE ACCORDED TO OTHERS' — no matching param in the pricing-competition vocabulary

§ 13-321 prohibitions are limited to a HIGHER price for tax-exempt food; § 13-322 disclosure applies to merchants generally but exempts insurance-regulated conduct, § 13-321-covered entities, financial institutions, and employee discounts (§ 13-322(B))

no penaltyMax: §§ 13-408(A) and 13-411(A) as amended each state 'THIS SECTION DOES NOT APPLY TO A VIOLATION OF § 13-321 OR § 13-322 OF THIS TITLE' — the title's private action and general $1,000 misdemeanor fine are expressly excluded; enforcement runs only through Division action under Subtitle 4 (MCPA penalties cross-referenced, not stated in this text)

plain-text extraction retains inline amendment markup (struck vs. inserted words indistinguishable, e.g. § 13-321(B) and Section 2's effective-date clause reading 'shall take effect from the date it is enacted shall take effect October 1, 2026'); coded values rely on the final-reading language
crossfiled with MD SB 387 per legiscan.js relations (not a replaced-by substitution)

entries.appliesTo: food retailers with employees covered by an existing collective bargaining agreement or memorandum of understanding

sources.enforcer: Labor & Employment § 4-406(C) — 'A PERSON MAY BRING AN ACTION TO RECOVER FOR INJURY OR LOSS SUSTAINED AS A RESULT OF A VIOLATION OF THIS SECTION'; § 4-406(D) — 'MAY ALSO SEEK, AND THE COURT MAY AWARD, REASONABLE ATTORNEY'S FEES'

flags: core requirement fits no listed duty or workforce param: Labor & Employment § 4-406(B) — 'A FOOD RETAILER MAY NOT IMPLEMENT AN ADMINISTRATIVE, OPERATIONAL, OR ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGE THAT DIMINISHES OR IMPAIRS ANY RIGHT OR BENEFIT GUARANTEED TO EMPLOYEES OF THE FOOD RETAILER UNDER AN EXISTING COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENT OR MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING UNLESS THE CHANGE IS NEGOTIATED AND MUTUALLY AGREED ON WITH THE EXCLUSIVE REPRESENTATIVE OF THE EMPLOYEES'
provision contains no AI-specific language; it is a worker-protection duty on employers enacted as part of the Protection From Predatory Pricing Act — workforce is the closest family
